PolicySet.Description: Cross-source corpus: operational access-control rules translated from GDPR, AMLD, PCI DSS, NIST SP 800-63B, SOX and DORA.

Rule.Description: GDPR Art. 17(1): the data subject has the right to erasure of personal data. Translation drops the Art. 17(3)(b) exception for legal retention obligations.
GDPR Art. 17(1) with Art. 17(3)(b) preserved: erasure permitted only when the record is not under a legal retention hold.
GDPR Art. 15: the data subject may read personal data held about them. Translation drops the Art. 23(1)(e) restriction that shields AML investigations.
GDPR Art. 15 with Art. 23(1)(e) preserved: subject access permitted only for records not flagged by a suspicious transaction report.
GDPR Art. 5(1)(c): personal data must be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary. Deny logging events that contain personal data without a documented purpose.
GDPR Art. 5(1)(e): personal data kept no longer than necessary. Organisational translation: permit purge of PII-bearing records older than 2 years.
GDPR Art. 6: deny transmission of personal data without a recorded lawful basis. Translation fails to recognise Art. 6(1)(c) legal obligation as a basis.

Policy.Description: Rules translated from the EU Anti-Money-Laundering Directive 2015/849.

Rule.Description: AMLD Art. 40: transaction records must be retained for five years after the business relationship ends. Deny erasure inside the retention window.
AMLD Art. 40 governed translation: customer-due-diligence records inside the retention window carry a legal hold; deny erasure while the hold is active.
AMLD Art. 39: the institution must not disclose to the customer that a suspicious transaction report has been filed. Deny data-subject reads of STR-flagged records.
AMLD Art. 39 governed translation: deny reads of STR-flagged KYC files. Pairs with the governed GDPR Art. 15 rule, which is scoped to non-flagged files.
AML investigation practice under AMLD Art. 32: financial-intelligence investigators may view full card numbers in flagged transactions.
Governed translation: investigator access to full card numbers requires a recorded legitimate business need (aligns with PCI DSS Req 3.3 exception).

Policy.Description: Rules translated from PCI DSS v4.0.

Rule.Description: PCI DSS Req 8.3.9: passwords must be changed at least every 90 days. Translation drops the sole-authentication-factor scope condition.
PCI DSS Req 8.3.9 governed translation: forced rotation applies only where the password is the sole authentication factor.
PCI DSS Req 10.2: all individual user access to cardholder data must be logged. The log event necessarily records the user identity.
PCI DSS Req 3.3: mask the PAN when displayed. Translation drops the exception for personnel with a legitimate business need.
PCI DSS Req 3.3 governed translation: deny full-PAN display only when no legitimate business need is recorded.

Policy.Description: Rules translated from NIST SP 800-63B digital identity guidelines.

Rule.Description: NIST SP 800-63B Sec. 5.1.1.2: do not force periodic password changes unless there is evidence of compromise.
NIST SP 800-63B governed translation: the no-forced-rotation rule applies only to credentials that are not the sole authentication factor.

Policy.Description: Rules translated from the Sarbanes-Oxley Act.

Rule.Description: SOX Sec. 802: audit workpapers must be retained for seven years. Deny purge inside the retention window.
DORA Art. 19: financial entities must report major ICT incidents to the competent authority. Incident reports routinely contain personal data of affected users.
DORA Art. 19 governed translation: transmission proceeds under GDPR Art. 6(1)(c) legal obligation, recorded as the lawful basis.

Policy.Description: Internal rules with no cross-source counterpart. Included so the corpus contains true negatives.

Rule.Description: HR managers may read employee leave requests.
Guest accounts may not modify system configuration.
